chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated that Ali ibn 'Inbasa narrated that Al-Hasan ibn Sulayman al-Malti, Nu'aym ibn Salih al-Matiri, and Darim ibn Qubaysa al-Nahshali narrated that Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrated from his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father, from his father Ali (peace be upon him), from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
I am the Treasure of Knowledge, and Ali is its Key. And whoever desires the Treasure, let him come to the Key.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: People of the House (implied context of Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Ali being described as the 'Key' to the Prophet's knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Twelve Imams in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, establishes the metaphysical hierarchy of knowledge where the Prophet serves as the 'storehouse' (khazana) and Imam Ali as the 'key' (miftah). It underscores the Shia doctrine that true esoteric and exoteric understanding of the Quran and Sunnah is inextricably linked to the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt, making Ali the indispensable gateway to divine wisdom.
